data.content:
## The BIP341 sighash - BIP143, finished

BIP143 fixed quadratic hashing and let signatures commit to the spent amount. BIP341 completes the thought - the signature now commits to **everything a signer could be lied to about**:

```
epoch              00
hash_type          00        (SIGHASH_DEFAULT)
version            02000000
locktime           00000000
sha_prevouts       SHA256(all outpoints)
sha_amounts        SHA256(all spent values)       ← every input
sha_scriptpubkeys  SHA256(all spent scripts)      ← every input, new
sha_sequences      SHA256(all nSequence)
sha_outputs        SHA256(all outputs)
spend_type         00        (key path, no annex)
input_index        00000000
```

**All inputs, not just this one.** BIP143 committed to *this* input's amount; a hardware wallet in a multi-input transaction could still be shown false data about the *other* inputs and tricked into overpaying fees. Here the amounts and scriptPubKeys of every spent coin are inside the hash - show a signer wrong data and the signature simply doesn't verify. The lying-host attack dies here.

**Single SHA-256 - and only the last one tagged.** The five midstates are plain single SHA-256: no double-hashing, no tags. The tag appears exactly once, on the final TapSighash digest. Note the fields enter *as serialized*: the scriptPubKey carries its length prefix `0x22` (34 bytes), the amount its full 8 LE bytes.

**SIGHASH_DEFAULT (0x00)** means ALL semantics with the type byte *omitted* from the signature - the common case got one byte shorter. And the input's position is finally explicit: `input_index`, no more inferring it from context.

The result feeds the TapSighash tagged hash - 32 bytes the Schnorr node signs.
data.title: Text Info Node

data.content:
## What two inputs change - and what they don't

Same machinery as the intro: x-only keys, tweak, TapSighash, Schnorr. Four things are new.

**Two messages, four bytes apart.** The five hash midstates are computed once - now spanning *both* coins and *both* outputs - and feed both Preimage Body nodes. The two finished messages are byte-identical except `input_index`: `00000000` vs `01000000`. Each signer therefore commits to the entire transaction - the other coin's amount and script included - so neither key can be shown a different version of the deal.

**Each input answers to its own lock.** Signature 2 is made with the *second* coin's tweaked key and verifies only against the *second* coin's output key. A perfectly valid signature checked against the wrong prevout is still a failed signature.

**One witness stack per input, in vin order.** No stack count byte - the input count already said how many. Each stack is the intro's same 66-byte shape (`01`, `40`, signature); the transaction simply carries two - one stack per input, none per output: outputs are committed data, they never sign. And every outpoint field stays fixed-width: spending vout 1 serializes as `01000000`, never as a bare `1` - one short byte and the whole transaction stops parsing.

**Verification now demands every prevout.** With one input, the Verify node's own scriptPubKey and amount *were* the complete prevout list. With two, the second coin's data exists nowhere in the transaction - so the *Taproot Prevouts (vin order)* section becomes mandatory, on both Verify nodes, identically. That's not a tool quirk: a taproot verifier consults the UTXO set for every coin spent.
data.title: Text Info Node
